info.title: Strait API
info.description: Deep-linking + deferred-match API. Two keys, both in Dashboard → Get started: the **secret key** (`Authorization: Bearer st_live_…`, server-side only) for the link endpoints, and the **publishable key** (`publishableKey: "st_pub_live_…"` in the JSON body, safe in apps and websites) for /v1/match, /v1/referrer, /v1/resolve, /v1/lookup, /v1/open and /v1/event. Rotating the publishable key keeps the previous key working for 7 days; responses to the old key carry `Strait-Key-Deprecated: <ISO expiry>`, and after that it gets 401. Operations marked `x-internal: true` are used by the Strait dashboard or by Stripe and are not part of the public API. Errors are always JSON `{ "error": "…" }`: malformed JSON bodies get 400, unknown /v1 routes 404.

tags.name: Links
tags.description: Create, read, update and deactivate short links (secret key, server-side).

tags.name: Analytics
tags.description: Taps, app opens, installs and conversions per link, channel, day, platform, campaign, country or UTM tag (secret key).

tags.name: Referrals
tags.description: Preview, not switched on yet: referral codes that ride on a tap and come back with the deferred match (secret key for the report).

tags.name: SDK
tags.description: Called by the Strait app and web SDKs with the publishable key: deferred matching, link resolution, open reports.

tags.name: Events
tags.description: Conversion and revenue events, attributed to the tap they came from.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Test webhooks, read their delivery history and redeliver.

tags.name: Domains
tags.description: Custom link domains (Starter and up, up to 5 per workspace): add one, read the DNS records and its status, remove it (secret key or dashboard session).

tags.name: Export
tags.description: Everything your workspace needs to leave Strait.

tags.name: Tools
tags.description: Dry runs and public checkers: simulate a tap, check App Links / Universal Links files, read a Live Tap Trace.

tags.name: Billing
tags.description: Used by the Strait dashboard and by Stripe, Paddle and Razorpay. Not part of the public API.

verified.description: true once Cloudflare reports the hostname and its certificate active and the ownership TXT record is in your DNS. Only then do links work on it.

status.description: live = serving your links. pending_dns = waiting for the CNAME and TXT records. issuing_certificate = DNS found, HTTPS certificate on its way. problem = needs attention (see message). not_created = saved while custom domains are read-only. unknown = the status could not be read right now.

message.description: Cloudflare's own words when something needs attention.

records.description: The DNS records to add at your DNS provider: one CNAME and the TXT records Cloudflare asks for.

slug.description: Unique among the workspace's active links (another workspace may use the same slug).

shortUrl.description: The link to share, on your workspace link domain: https://<handle>.strait.link/<slug>. Links live on their workspace's host; the bare root only answers a slug no other workspace uses.

tenantId.description: The workspace the link belongs to.

webTapId.description: This link's override of the workspace setting for strait_click on web pages (see NewLink). Absent = the workspace setting (on unless turned off).

campaign.description: Analytics campaign; defaults to longUrl's utm_campaign.

health.description: Link health (ADR 0057): the last background check of the destinations and store listings. `status` ok | attention | unknown; each problem has `field`, `url`, `verdict` (broken | at_risk) and the checker's `summary`. Absent until the first check.

passwordProtected.description: Present (true) when the link has a password.

blockedReason.description: Set when the link was disabled under the Acceptable Use Policy.

expiredAction.description: Where a tap goes once the link has expired. page = the "This link has expired" page (410). store = Google Play on Android / the App Store on iPhone (302, from your app configuration; the Play install referrer carries the tap); computers, and phones whose store is not configured, get the expired-link web page, else the expired page. url = 302 to expiredUrl. Absent/null = the workspace setting (Settings → When a link expires; default page).

expiredUrl.description: This link's expired-link web page (https); absent = the workspace's.

startsAt.description: epoch ms. Scheduled go-live: before it, taps get notLiveAction. Absent = live now.

notLiveAction.description: Where a tap goes BEFORE startsAt (the link is not live yet). page = a branded "Coming soon" page. store = Google Play on Android / the App Store on iPhone (302, from your app configuration); computers, and phones whose store is not configured, get notLiveUrl, else the page. url = 302 to notLiveUrl. Taps before go-live are not recorded and never billed; link-preview bots still get the preview card. Absent = page.

url.description: https; passes the same unsafe-destination check as longUrl

countryRules.description: Up to 5 rules, first match wins. When the tap's country (from Cloudflare, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) is in a rule's countries, the rule's url replaces the web / fallback destination (iosFallbackUrl, androidFallbackUrl, desktopUrl, longUrl as a web page, the workspace fallback). Opening the app and the app-store hand-offs are unchanged. The country is also stored with the tap as its 2-letter code, for analytics (group=country).

legacyHost.description: Imported from Firebase Dynamic Links: the old host (lower case, no https:// or path). Goes with legacyCode. When an app that keeps this host as an associated domain opens https://<legacyHost>/<legacyCode>, /v1/resolve finds this link by the old host + code before the slug, so the same code from two old hosts, or an old code and a newer slug, never clash. One active link per old host + code in a workspace (409 otherwise).

legacyCode.description: The old Firebase short code on legacyHost, exactly as it was (case-sensitive).

referralCode.description: Preview (referrals not switched on yet). Only in the POST /v1/links answer, and only when the code was saved. Not returned by the list, get or update endpoints yet.

longUrl.description: https only. The app receives its path + query as the in-app route.

iosFallbackUrl.description: iPhone without the app: this page instead of longUrl (https).

androidFallbackUrl.description: Android without the app (website mode): this page instead of longUrl (https).

desktopUrl.description: Desktop browsers go here instead of longUrl (https).

webTapId.description: Taps sent to a web page (desktopUrl, the fallbacks, longUrl as a web page, a country rule, the workspace fallback) get this tap's id added as strait_click=<tap id>, the same id the app hand-off and the Play referrer carry, so @straitlink/web (and the React Native / Flutter web builds) count a web open joined to the tap. Existing query params (UTMs included) are kept as they are. On by default for the workspace. false turns it off for this link (a page that rejects unknown query params); true keeps it on even when the workspace turned it off.

variants.description: A/B test: web taps are split across these https destinations by weight (e.g. two with weight 1 = 50/50). Each url passes the same unsafe-destination check as longUrl.

campaign.description: Campaign name for analytics. Defaults to longUrl's utm_campaign when omitted (and follows it when longUrl changes).

expiresAt.description: After this, the link stops opening its destination; expiredAction decides where taps go. Omit for never.

expiredAction.description: Where a tap goes once the link has expired. page = the "This link has expired" page (410). store = Google Play on Android / the App Store on iPhone (302, from your app configuration; the Play install referrer carries the tap); computers, and phones whose store is not configured, get the expired-link web page, else the expired page. url = 302 to expiredUrl. Omit to use the workspace setting (default page).

expiredUrl.description: https. Required with expiredAction url; with store it is where computers go. Passes the same unsafe-destination check as longUrl.

startsAt.description: Scheduled go-live. Before it, taps get notLiveAction; must be before expiresAt. Omit for live now.

notLiveAction.description: Where a tap goes BEFORE startsAt (the link is not live yet). page = a branded "Coming soon" page. store = Google Play on Android / the App Store on iPhone (302, from your app configuration); computers, and phones whose store is not configured, get notLiveUrl, else the page. url = 302 to notLiveUrl. Taps before go-live are not recorded and never billed; link-preview bots still get the preview card. Omit for page.

notLiveUrl.description: https. Required with notLiveAction url; with store it is where computers go. Passes the same unsafe-destination check as longUrl.

url.description: https; passes the same unsafe-destination check as longUrl

countryRules.description: Up to 5 rules, first match wins. When the tap's country (from Cloudflare, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) is in a rule's countries, the rule's url replaces the web / fallback destination (iosFallbackUrl, androidFallbackUrl, desktopUrl, longUrl as a web page, the workspace fallback). Opening the app and the app-store hand-offs are unchanged. The country is also stored with the tap as its 2-letter code, for analytics (group=country).

legacyHost.description: Imported from Firebase Dynamic Links: the old host (lower case, no https:// or path). Goes with legacyCode. When an app that keeps this host as an associated domain opens https://<legacyHost>/<legacyCode>, /v1/resolve finds this link by the old host + code before the slug, so the same code from two old hosts, or an old code and a newer slug, never clash. One active link per old host + code in a workspace (409 otherwise).

legacyCode.description: The old Firebase short code on legacyHost, exactly as it was (case-sensitive).

referralCode.description: Preview (referrals not switched on yet; until then the field is ignored). This link's referral code: 1 to 64 letters, digits, - or _. Every tap carries it unless the tap has its own ?strait_ref=; it comes back as `referralCode` in the deferred-match answer. Don't use an email address or phone number. Not accepted by the batch or update endpoints yet.

password.description: Optional: visitors must enter it before the link opens (link-preview bots still get the preview card). Stored hashed, never returned; the link shows passwordProtected: true.

FunnelByPlatform.description: People at this step by the platform of their tap (tablets and unknown devices are `other`).

link_id.description: The link's id, or null for the whole workspace.

steps.description: Always four, in order, never increasing: clicked, app_or_store, opened_app, reached_screen.

split.description: opened_app only: already had the app, or installed it first (a matched install names the tap, whatever opened the app after it).

certainty.description: reached_screen only: exact (app link, direct open, Play Install Referrer, clipboard token) or estimated (iPhone device match).

phone_clicks.description: Taps minus the `computer` exit: the base of step 2.

exits.description: Who left before step 2, in this order: computer (sent to your website), phone_website (a phone sent to your website), in_app_browser (saw the open-in-app page inside Instagram, WhatsApp… and did not press it), other (not tracked).

drops.description: store_no_open (after app_or_store: sent to the store, no app open seen) and open_failed (after opened_app: the app opened but the link did not resolve; `reasons` such as expired, not_found, network, no_match, unknown).

untied_failed_opens.description: App opens that failed and name no tap (the link expired or was not found, so no tap was recorded): no step can hold them. With a filter, only those whose link fits it.

installs.description: Installs of the period (GET /v1/analytics `installs`), by where the tap was. credited = from_period_clicks + from_earlier_clicks + from_link_no_click; total = credited + organic; credited = exact + estimated (estimated: an iPhone device match). from_period_clicks = steps[2].split.installed.

from_link_no_click.description: Credited to a link, but its tap is not in the record (an iPhone match entry, or a tap older than retention).

tied_to_click.description: from_period_clicks + from_earlier_clicks: installs tied to a recorded click. credited = tied_to_click + from_link_no_click.

tied_estimated.description: Of tied_to_click, estimated (an iPhone device match).

estimated_from_earlier_clicks.description: Estimated installs whose click was before the period (why iPhone installs can exceed this period's iPhone app opens).

click_to_install.description: Time from click to install: the middle value over tied installs whose first open came through the store (n of them). A first open that came directly from the link (app link / custom scheme: the app was already installed) is no install time and is counted apart. n + first_open_from_link = tied_to_click.

by_platform.description: The same parts per platform of the install (android, ios, other); each part adds up across platforms. from_period_clicks per platform is never above steps[2].by_platform for it.

match_certainty.description: The two exact / estimated numbers, each named by what it counts: `installs` = credited installs (exact: Play referrer, clipboard, app hand-off; estimated: an iPhone device match); `reached_screen` = clicks that reached the screen (= steps[3]). They count different things and never add up to each other.

website_opens.description: Clicks whose website reported the landing (web SDK reportWebOpen): they opened your website, not the app. Never an app open or an install.

test_data_left_out.description: Clicks and installs of Strait's own test links (our smoke / QA / load checks in our own workspaces) in this range, left out of every number above. Always 0 for your workspace.

revenue.description: Revenue after a tap: POST /v1/event values in the period that carry a tap of this slice (the tap may be older), per ISO currency (never summed across currencies).

days.description: Taps and reached_screen per local day (`tz`) of the range, every day listed (zeros included); null for a range over 400 days. The days add up to steps 1 and 4.

did_something.description: Of reached_screen, how many sent at least one event (POST /v1/event) with that tap; null when your app has never sent an event.

unmatched_first_opens.description: First opens after an install we could not connect to any tap; whole workspace only (null with a filter).

installs_without_click.description: Installs matched to a link but not to one tap.

expired_taps.description: Taps on expired links: in no step.

previous.description: With compare=1 on a paid plan: the period of equal length just before (null on Free).

plan.description: Free sees every number for 30 days; `locked` names what a paid plan adds (compare, campaign_results, csv, long_range).

taps.description: Taps on live links (not deferred-match entries, not taps on expired links).

billableTaps.description: Of those, the taps that count toward your plan (a repeat of the same tap within seconds is not billed).

appOpens.description: App opens reported by the SDKs that came from one of your links.

installs.description: Installs tied to one of your links (organic installs are not counted). The installs and first-open reports are merged: reports naming the same tap are one install, the same definition as the dashboard.

conversions.description: POST /v1/event events tied to one of your links (directly or through their tap).

revenue.description: Event values summed per currency code (upper case; '' when an event gave none). Currencies are never added together.

key.description: The group value: a UTC day (YYYY-MM-DD), a channel (whatsapp, instagram, direct…), a link id, a platform (android, ios, desktop), the link's campaign, a 2-letter country code (IN, US…) or a UTM tag's value as tagged. null for group=campaign, country or utm_* means no value: the link has no campaign, the country was not known, or the tap had no such tag (also rows with no tap, such as an install matched to a link without its tap). An app or SDK version as reported (4.12.0, 0.9.0) for group=app_version or sdk_version, where null holds every tap and conversion and the opens from an SDK that sent no version.

Tap.description: One tap, joined to its first app open and its install. Fields the tap does not have are null.

source.description: web (a tap in a browser) or an SDK source

billable.description: false for a repeat within 10 seconds

opens.description: App opens joined to this tap

appVersion.description: App version that first opened this tap (else its install), as the SDK reported it

sdkVersion.description: Strait SDK version of that open

MatchInfo.description: Present only when matched (absent otherwise, never null): how this install was matched and how sure we are, in plain terms. install_referrer / clipboard = exact (Google Play or a single-use paste token named the tap). fingerprint = an iPhone device-signal match (matchMethod exact_ext or exact_core): probable, because two people with the same iPhone model on one network look alike; high is reserved for the scored matcher's top band once it is enabled. test = a test-mode answer (always probable: the newest tap in the window, not proof of this device). Gate sensitive deep links (referral rewards, invites) on exact. Can be absent on a replay of an install recorded before Oct 2026. matchMethod and confidence are unchanged.

matchMethod.description: How it matched. 'clipboard' = a claimed paste-handoff token (POST /v1/handoff/claim). 'test' = test mode: a debug re-check (record:false) answered from the workspace's open test window (Dashboard -> Get started -> Test mode). 'scored' is reserved for the scored iPhone matcher, which is not enabled yet.

confidence.description: Scored matches only (matchMethod 'scored'): 'high' or 'medium'. Null for every other answer of /v1/match.

clickId.description: When matched: the id of the tap this install came from. The SDKs remember it and send it with conversion events (/v1/event `clickId`).

referralCode.description: Preview (referrals not switched on yet). Present only when matched and the tap carried a referral code: the tap's ?strait_ref=, else its link's referralCode. Absent otherwise (never null). The SDKs pass it to your app as `referralCode` on the deferred link (contract B21).

test.description: Present (true) only on a test-mode answer: a debug re-check (record:false) while the workspace's test window was open. matched:false then carries reason no_tap (no tap since the window opened; tap a link and check again), other_device (the window belongs to the first phone that checked in) or not_found. A test answer never carries clickId. Absent otherwise.

deviceMatching.description: The workspace's Device matching switch (Dashboard Settings -> iPhone installs; opt-in, off by default).

pasteHandoff.description: The workspace's Paste handoff switch (opt-in, off by default). When true and this lookup found no match, the SDK checks the clipboard for the one-time handoff link and claims it (POST /v1/handoff/claim).

ios.description: /v1/match with platform 'ios' only: the workspace's current iPhone deferred-link choice (device matching and/or paste handoff, the customer's choice in the dashboard; opt-in, off by default), read live on every lookup so a change in the dashboard applies without an app release. The SDKs never store it (contract B19).

ipv4Match.description: iPhone first-launch check only (platform 'ios', openId sent, record not false): present when this ask came over IPv6 and found no tap (reason no_candidate). The phone may have tapped over IPv4: the SDK sends the same request (same openId, same fields) once more to this IPv4-only URL. A match there answers exact_ext with reason ip_family (match.confidence probable, never exact) and the install recorded by the first ask becomes matched (counted once). Absent otherwise.

reasons.description: Why the matcher matched or refused, as short codes (never personal data). Exact matcher: exact_ext, exact_core, no_candidate, ambiguous (two identical-looking taps for different links: Strait refuses rather than guesses), race_lost (another lookup already took this tap), device_matching_off (the workspace turned iPhone install matching off), ip_family (matched across IPv4 / IPv6: the IPv4-only probe host). Paste handoff: clipboard, handoff_unknown, handoff_used, handoff_expired. Scored matches add signal codes (e.g. ipv6_64, ip_exact, asn, lang_full, dt_42s). New codes may be added; treat unknown codes as informational.

get.description: Without `limit`/`cursor`: every active link as a JSON array (unchanged). With either: one page `{ links, nextCursor }`, newest first; pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` until it is null. `status=paused` lists paused links instead (turned off with DELETE, PATCH `isActive: false` or the dashboard; links disabled for abuse are not listed), always as pages.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1–100 (larger values are capped at 100). Default 50 when paging.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque `nextCursor` from the previous page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `active` (default) or `paused`. Paused links come back as pages; turn one back on with PATCH `isActive: true`.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Only links with this exact tag (works with or without paging). 1–100 characters, no `"` or `\`.

200.description: Links (array), or a page when limit/cursor is given

400.description: Invalid limit, cursor or status

post.summary: Create a link

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional (ADR 0055). Retry with the same key and the same body to get the first answer back (header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`) instead of running again. 1 to 255 of `[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]`, kept 24 hours per workspace and endpoint. 5xx, 429 and 402 answers are not kept.

201.description: Created: the link, with the shortUrl to share

400.description: Invalid field, destination_blocked (a URL failed the unsafe-destination check; `field` names which one, e.g. `iosFallbackUrl` or `variants[1].url`), or invalid_idempotency_key

402.description: Plan limit reached (this month's new links, or taps over twice the plan). Existing links keep working. Body: `{ error, reason: "links" | "clicks", upgradeUrl }` ("clicks" = the monthly tap limit).

409.description: An active link with this slug already exists in this workspace, or `idempotency_key_in_use`: a request with the same Idempotency-Key is still running (Retry-After: 1)

422.description: `idempotency_key_reused`: the Idempotency-Key was used in the last 24 hours with a different body

429.description: New-account limit: a workspace younger than 24 hours can create 25 links. It lifts by itself; Retry-After says when. Body: `{ error: "new_account_limit", reason: "links", message, limit, resetsAt }`.

post.summary: Create up to 500 links in one call
post.description: For imports and migrations. Each item passes the same checks as POST /v1/links (slug rules, https destinations, the unsafe-destination check, plan limits) and gets its own result; a bad item never fails the batch. A slug already used in the workspace (or earlier in the same batch) is a per-item 409, so re-running an import is safe. The response is 200 whenever the request itself is valid: read `results[i].ok`. Items past a plan limit get 402.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional (ADR 0055). Retry with the same key and the same body to get the first answer back (header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`) instead of running again. 1 to 255 of `[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]`, kept 24 hours per workspace and endpoint. 5xx, 429 and 402 answers are not kept.

200.description: One result per item, in order, plus totals

status.description: What POST /v1/links would have answered: 201, 400, 402 or 409.

field.description: For destination_blocked: the field holding the listed URL (longUrl, iosFallbackUrl, androidFallbackUrl, desktopUrl, expiredUrl, notLiveUrl, countryRules[i].url, variants[i].url).

results.error: slug already exists in this workspace

400.description: `links` is missing, empty, or has more than 500 items

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: The link's slug: the part after your link domain, e.g. `summer`

200.description: The link (with shortUrl)

404.description: No active link with this slug in the key's workspace

patch.description: Send only the fields to change. null clears expiresAt (never expires), expiredAction (back to the workspace setting), expiredUrl, startsAt (live now), notLiveAction (the coming-soon page), notLiveUrl and countryRules (null or [] = none; a list replaces all rules). `isActive` is sent on its own: `false` pauses the link (same as DELETE). `true` answers the active link with this slug if there is one (safe to retry; check its longUrl), else turns the most recently paused one back on (taps follow within 30 seconds, like any edit). A link disabled for abuse cannot be turned back on (409 link_blocked).

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: The link's slug: the part after your link domain, e.g. `summer`

expiredAction.description: Where taps go once the link has expired (see NewLink); null = the workspace setting.

expiredUrl.description: https; required when expiredAction is url.

startsAt.description: Scheduled go-live (see NewLink); null = live now.

notLiveAction.description: Where taps go before startsAt (see NewLink); null = the coming-soon page.

notLiveUrl.description: https; required when notLiveAction is url.

isActive.description: Send alone. false = pause, true = turn the paused link back on.

webTapId.description: strait_click on web pages for this link (see NewLink); null = follow the workspace setting.

url.description: https; passes the same unsafe-destination check as longUrl

countryRules.description: Replaces all country rules (see NewLink); null or [] removes them.

200.description: Updated

400.description: Invalid field, isActive sent with other fields, or destination_blocked (a URL failed the unsafe-destination check; `field` names which one; with isActive: true the link stays paused)

404.description: Not found (with isActive: true: no paused or active link with this slug)

409.description: isActive: true refused: link_blocked (disabled for abuse) or slug_in_use (the database refused: a link created at the same moment, or the same Firebase link is on)

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: The link's slug: the part after your link domain, e.g. `summer`

404.description: No active link with this slug in the key's workspace

get.summary: Get a branded QR code for a link
get.description: A print-ready QR code (PNG or SVG) that opens the link's short URL. It uses the workspace's QR style (Dashboard → Settings → QR codes: colour, background, app icon in the middle); query parameters override it for this one code. By default the code adds `utm_source=qr`, so scans show as the **qr** channel in analytics (an existing utm_source on the link is kept). The code must be darker than its background with a contrast of at least 3:1, or the request is refused with 400. With a logo the code uses error correction H. The logo is the app icon from Settings: PNG, JPEG or WebP in SVG codes, PNG only in PNG codes; X-Strait-Qr-Logo says whether it was embedded. Rate limit: 60 codes a minute per workspace; PNG renders also share a server-wide budget (large PNGs may get 429, retry or use SVG).

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: The link's slug: the part after your link domain, e.g. `summer`

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Image format

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Width and height in pixels

parameters.name: margin
parameters.description: Quiet zone around the code, in modules

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Code colour as hex (`1f2937`, or `%231f2937`). Default: the workspace's QR colour, else black.

parameters.name: background
parameters.description: Background colour as hex. Default: the workspace's QR background, else white.

parameters.name: logo
parameters.description: Put the app icon in the middle. Default: the workspace's QR setting.

parameters.name: preset
parameters.description: Start from a saved QR style (Settings → QR codes) instead of the workspace default; color, background and logo still override it. Unknown id: 400.

parameters.name: track
parameters.description: Add utm_source=qr so scans count as the qr channel

parameters.name: download
parameters.description: true: Content-Disposition attachment (a browser saves the file)

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Dashboard sessions only: the workspace id (a secret key already names its workspace)

200.description: The QR code

X-Strait-Qr-Url.description: The exact URL encoded in the code

X-Strait-Qr-Logo.description: embedded · off · no_icon (no app icon in Settings) · unavailable (icon unreachable or not PNG/JPEG/WebP ≤ 512 KB) · png_needs_png_icon (use format=svg, or a PNG icon)

image/svg+xml.example: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1024" height="1024" viewBox="0 0 37 37" shape-rendering="crispEdges"><rect width="37" height="37" fill="#ffffff"/><path fill="#1f2937" d="M2 2h7v1h-7z…"/></svg>

400.description: Invalid parameter, or colours that would not scan (code lighter than the background, or contrast under 3:1)

401.description: Missing or invalid secret key / session

404.description: No active link with this slug in the workspace

429.description: More than 60 codes a minute for this workspace (Retry-After: 1), or PNG rendering is busy server-wide (Retry-After: 2; SVG is not limited by it)

get.summary: Download every QR code of a campaign as one ZIP
get.description: A ZIP with one QR code per **live** link whose campaign is `campaign` (case-insensitive, the same match as the dashboard's links filter), named `<slug>-qr.<format>` and sorted by slug. Same style rules as GET /v1/links/{slug}/qr: the workspace default or `preset`, overridden by color / background / logo, refused (400) when it would not scan. SVG by default (vector, for print). At most 500 codes as SVG, or 50 as PNG at up to 1024 px. Rate limit: 3 ZIPs a minute per workspace; one PNG ZIP at a time server-wide.

parameters.name: campaign
parameters.description: The links' campaign name, e.g. `diwali_sale`

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Image format of every code

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Width and height in pixels (PNG: at most 1024)

parameters.name: margin

post.summary: Record a conversion / revenue event
post.description: From an app or website send `publishableKey`; from a server you may instead authenticate with the secret key as a Bearer token. `clickId` names the tap the conversion came from: every tap gets a unique id (a UUID, sent with the tap's redirect and passed to your app with the open), which the mobile SDKs remember from the attributed app open and attach for 7 days. It is kept only when it is a tap of this workspace; otherwise it is ignored and the event is still recorded. Each new event (not an eventId retry) is sent to your webhooks subscribed to `app.event`, with `data` and `sentWith` (publishable_key or secret_key: trust revenue sent from your server) and `userId` / `userIdHashed` (your user, when set). Webhook sends for events sent with the publishable key are capped per workspace (600 burst, then 10 a second): past that, they are still recorded but not sent. Events sent with the secret key are not capped.

linkId.description: Optional: with a known clickId it is filled in from that tap

clickId.description: The id of the tap this conversion came from (the mobile SDKs fill it in)

eventId.description: Optional idempotency id, e.g. your order id: a retry with the same eventId is accepted but stored once. An event sent with your secret key replaces one sent first with the publishable key (keeping its tap and link when it has none) and is sent to your webhooks again, so a receiver de-duplicates on eventId + sentWith; nothing replaces a secret-key event.

data.description: Optional custom key-values (at most 20, 2 KB as JSON) passed to the app.event webhook. Not stored with the event; kept 30 days with the webhook delivery. Do not send personal data your receiver does not need.

userId.description: Optional: your own user id (the SDKs' setUserId), passed to the app.event webhook as `userId` so you can join events to your users. Not stored with the event; kept 30 days with the webhook delivery. An email (any `@`) or phone number (only digits, spaces and + ( ) . -, 8-15 digits) is replaced by its SHA-256 hex (of the lower-cased email / of the digits) and sent with `userIdHashed: true`; the SDKs do this on the device. Trimmed; empty, longer than 128 characters or with control characters = dropped (the event is still recorded).

userIdHashed.description: True when `userId` is already a SHA-256 hex of an email or phone (the SDKs set it).

202.description: Accepted. `clickId` echoes the tap id that was stored, or null when none was given or it was not a tap of this workspace.

linkId.description: The linkId kept for this event: yours if it is one of your links, else the clickId tap's link; null when neither (unknown ids are dropped, the event is still recorded)

get.description: Fetches https://<domain>/.well-known/assetlinks.json and /.well-known/apple-app-site-association (plus the legacy /apple-app-site-association) and explains each finding with a severity and a fix. No key needed. Rate-limited (10 per minute per IP); results cached 60 s per domain; CORS only for https://straitlink.in, https://app.straitlink.in and http://localhost:<port>. Only public domains: IP addresses and names that resolve to private/reserved addresses are refused (400). https only, at most 5 redirects, 5 s, 256 KB. It checks the files on the domain, not how a particular phone behaves.

post.summary: Is my app link broken? (public tool)
post.description: Opens one pasted link the way an Android phone, an iPhone and a desktop browser would (following redirects, reading app and store hand-offs) and says what each device gets: the app, the store, the web, or a dead end. Works on any provider (page.link, Branch, AppsFlyer, Strait, your own domain). No key needed. POST so the link never lands in an access log; nothing is stored. Rate-limited (10 per minute per IP, shared with /v1/tools/app-links, and 60 checks a minute across all visitors); CORS only for https://straitlink.in, https://app.straitlink.in and http://localhost:<port>. Only public https links on a domain name: IP addresses, private networks and odd ports are refused (400). At most 8 hops per device, 5 s each.

200.description: The report. `verdict`: ok | at_risk | broken | unchecked. Each platform result has an `outcome` (app | store | web | dead | loop | error), a one-line `summary`, the `hops` it took, and the `app` / `store` it reached.

example.headline: This link is broken on every device.

post.summary: Send a test event to a webhook
post.description: Delivers a `ping` event to the webhook right now (even if paused) and returns the receiver's HTTP status and the time it took (never its response body). Not stored or retried. Every delivery is signed: `X-Strait-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>" with the webhook secret>` — recompute it and refuse timestamps more than 5 minutes old. It is the only signature header. Other headers: X-Strait-Event, X-Strait-Delivery (stable across retries — de-duplicate on it), X-Strait-Attempt. Events: link.clicked, app.opened, install.matched, referral.converted and app.event (POST /v1/event). Webhook URLs must be public https endpoints: private, loopback, link-local and CGNAT addresses are refused when saved and again at every delivery, when the connection is made (after DNS resolution).

parameters.description: The webhook id (Dashboard → Settings → Webhooks)

get.description: Everything your workspace needs to leave Strait, streamed as a download. Auth: a secret key (a publishable key gets 401), or `token` from POST /v1/export/token (one use, 60 seconds; this is how the dashboard downloads). `part=links`: NDJSON, one link per line (active and inactive). `part=taps`: CSV of every tap joined to its first app open and install, oldest first, no date cap. `part=events`: CSV of every conversion / revenue event, oldest first; channel, campaign and variant come from the tap the event is attributed to (when it has a click_id). `part=webhooks`: JSON of your webhook configuration (url, events, active, createdAt) — signing secrets are never exported. `part=worker`: a single-file Cloudflare Worker (`export default { fetch }`) that keeps your active links redirecting by device (Android / iPhone-iPad / desktop) without Strait.

post.summary: Redeliver a webhook delivery
post.description: Re-queues one delivery (typically `failed`, after all retries) and sends it right away to the webhook's current URL, with the same X-Strait-Delivery id. Its attempt count starts over, so it gets the full retry schedule again. Refused (409) when it was already delivered, or while it is being sent (younger than 2 minutes, or claimed by a worker right now).
